newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks jump in morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks jump in morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks started the Chinese Year of the Ox on a strong note on Monday, with the Hang Seng Index jumping 196 points, or 1.44 percent, to 13,856 at the opening.
A higher opening on the first day of the Lunar New Year is labelled a "red opening", red symbolising luck.
The blue-chip index later reduced its gains to trade 99.16 points higher at 13,759.66. Turnover was HK$1.51 billion after the first half hour of trade.

"Last week we had the FOMC (U.S. Federal Open Market Committee) meeting and then the U.S. employment data and both of them indicated that the Fed won't touch interest rates for the moment. We have a few weeks to relax," said Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities.
"Most investors will think it's lucky -- it's traditional," said Tam. "If the market is good for the whole day it is good for the whole year."
Shares in HSBC Holdings led the market's rise on Monday. The stock gained HK$5.50 to HK$189.50 after jumping to an all-time high of HK$191.50 earlier.
"It's going to HK$200 short term, either before or after its results," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
HSBC is due to release its 1996 results on March 3.
Property stocks failed to participate in the morning's rally with shares in Sun Hung Kai Properties down HK$0.50 at HK$92.50 and Henderson Land off HK$0.50 at HK$73.00.
Analysts said the Hang Seng index was likely to test 14,000 points this week, but without a rise in the property sector was unlikely to break through that level.
"Although the market is strong, there is not that much to drive it up too quickly," said Rossiter. "Slow and steady is probably the best policy."
